title: Articles: zero article and generic reference
titleVi: Mạo từ: không dùng mạo từ và danh từ khái quát
summary: Khi nào bỏ mạo từ hoàn toàn, cách dùng the với tổ chức và địa danh, và the + tính từ chỉ nhóm người.
whyItMatters: Ở band 7.5–8.0, lỗi mạo từ là thứ duy nhất còn giữ điểm Grammatical Accuracy ở mức 7. Người học thường thêm *the* trước danh từ khái quát (*the society*, *the unemployment*) hoặc trước địa danh (*the Mount Everest*), và bỏ *the* ở những chỗ bắt buộc (*in hospital* với nghĩa bệnh nhân). Đây là nhóm lỗi mà giám khảo nhận ra ngay lập tức.

sections.heading: Institutions versus buildings
body: When a place is used **for its purpose**, English drops the article: *go to school* (as a pupil), *go to university*, *be in hospital* (as a patient), *be in prison* (as a prisoner), *go to church* (to worship), *go to bed*, *go to work*, *go home*.
When you mean the **building**, keep the article: *The school was built in 1920*, *I went to the school to meet the head teacher*, *She was in the hospital visiting her aunt.*
The same distinction explains *at home* versus *in the house*, and *at sea* (as a sailor) versus *on the sea* (a boat). The article is not decoration: it changes the meaning.

rows: He is in the school building.
She is in the hospital (as a visitor).
He went to prison for fraud.
They go to church on Sundays.
Classes start at 8; I go to university.

sections.heading: the + adjective: whole groups of people
body: **the + adjective** creates a plural noun meaning a social group: *the poor, the rich, the elderly, the unemployed, the homeless, the disabled, the young.* The verb is plural: *The elderly need better access to healthcare.*
The same pattern produces nationalities: *the French, the Dutch, the Vietnamese, the Japanese*. These take a plural verb even though they look singular: *The French are famous for their cuisine.*

Do not add a noun: *the poor people* is not wrong but shifts the meaning to specific poor people you can see. For the social category, *the poor* is the precise form — and it is exactly the register Task 2 needs.

examples.right: The unemployed receive a monthly allowance.
Housing policy has done little for the homeless.
examples.note: **the + adjective** as the object of a preposition.

examples.right: The young are more likely to rent than to buy.
examples.wrong: The youngs are more likely to rent than to buy.
examples.note: Never add *-s*; the adjective already carries the plural meaning.

sections.heading: the with unique objects, inventions and instruments
body: Singular nouns that are unique in context take **the**: *the sun, the moon, the sky, the sea, the government, the economy, the environment, the internet.* This is why Task 2 environmental writing is full of *the*: *the planet, the climate, the ozone layer*.

For inventions and machines, **the + singular** refers to the whole class: *The bicycle is the most efficient vehicle ever invented.* Musical instruments follow the same rule: *play the piano, play the guitar* — while sports and games take no article: *play football, play chess*.
Two more fixed patterns: **the + comparative**, as in *the more we consume, the more we waste*, and **the + decade**, as in *the 1990s*, *the early 2000s*.

rows: The telephone changed how we work.
She plays the violin in an orchestra.
The higher the income, the greater the consumption.

sections.heading: Names with and without the
body: Most place names take **no article**: cities, countries (*Vietnam, Japan, Brazil*), continents, single mountains (*Everest, Fuji*), single lakes, streets, airports, universities named after a place (*Hanoi University*).

**the** appears with: rivers (*the Mekong, the Thames*), seas and oceans (*the Pacific*), mountain ranges (*the Andes, the Himalayas*), groups of islands (*the Philippines, the Maldives*), and country names containing *republic, kingdom, states, union* or a plural (*the UK, the US, the Netherlands, the Czech Republic*).

Institutions follow the same logic. **the** with organisations, newspapers and famous buildings: *the UN, the EU, the Guardian, the Louvre*. **no article** with companies, shops and banks: *Samsung, HSBC, Vinamilk*.

rows: the Philippines, the Netherlands, the UK
the United Nations, the European Union
Oxford Street, Tran Hung Dao Street

sections.heading: Zero article: the academic default
body: Generic statements — the backbone of Task 2 — use **no article** with plural countables and uncountables: *Governments should invest in education*, *Research suggests that pollution reduces life expectancy*, *Data from the survey indicate a clear trend.*

Fixed prepositional phrases also drop the article: *in conclusion, in practice, in theory, on average, by contrast, at present, for example, in addition, in general.* Adding *the* to these is one of the most visible article errors in essays: *In the conclusion* is wrong when you mean *In conclusion*.

Languages, school subjects, meals, sports, seasons and transport take no article: *She speaks Japanese*, *He studies economics*, *We had lunch at noon*, *in summer*, *by train*. Note *in the summer* is also correct when you mean a specific summer.

examples.right: In conclusion, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
examples.wrong: In the conclusion, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.

examples.right: Society has become more dependent on technology.
examples.wrong: The society has become more dependent on technology.
examples.note: *society* as an abstraction takes no article.

examples.right: She is studying economics at university.

commonMistakes.wrong: My grandfather is in the hospital with pneumonia.
commonMistakes.right: My grandfather is in hospital with pneumonia.
commonMistakes.why: Khi nói về **bệnh nhân**, tiếng Anh bỏ mạo từ: *in hospital*. *In the hospital* chỉ đúng khi nói về tòa nhà hoặc người đến thăm.

commonMistakes.wrong: We climbed the Mount Everest last year.
commonMistakes.right: We climbed Mount Everest last year.
commonMistakes.why: Tên **một ngọn núi riêng lẻ** không dùng *the*: *Everest, Fuji*. Chỉ dãy núi mới dùng: *the Andes, the Himalayas*.

commonMistakes.wrong: I usually go to the bed at eleven.
commonMistakes.right: I usually go to bed at eleven.
commonMistakes.why: *Bed* ở đây là **hoạt động ngủ**, không phải cái giường cụ thể, nên bỏ mạo từ — giống *go to school*, *go to work*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The society is becoming more individualistic.
commonMistakes.why: Danh từ trừu tượng dùng khái quát **không có mạo từ**. *The society* chỉ đúng khi nói về một tổ chức cụ thể.

commonMistakes.wrong: She plays the tennis every weekend.
commonMistakes.why: Môn thể thao **không dùng mạo từ** (*play tennis, play football*), trong khi nhạc cụ lại **bắt buộc** có *the* (*play the piano*). Đây là cặp dễ lẫn.

ieltsTips: Bắt đầu kết bài bằng `In conclusion,` — không bao giờ `In the conclusion,`. Đây là lỗi mạo từ bị trừ điểm thấy rõ nhất.
Câu khái quát trong Task 2 dùng danh từ số nhiều hoặc không đếm được **không mạo từ**: `Governments should fund public transport.`
Khi viết về môi trường, dùng `the` cho vật thể duy nhất: `the planet`, `the climate`, `the ozone layer` — nhưng `Nature` thì không.
Kiểm tra tên riêng trước khi nộp: thành phố, quốc gia, đường phố, trường đại học hầu như **không** có `the`.

exercises.question: After the accident, he spent three weeks in ___ hospital.
exercises.explanation: Với nghĩa **nằm viện điều trị**, bỏ mạo từ: *in hospital*.

exercises.question: ___ unemployment has risen sharply since 2020.
exercises.explanation: Danh từ trừu tượng không đếm được dùng khái quát → không mạo từ.

exercises.question: She has played ___ violin since she was six.
exercises.explanation: Nhạc cụ luôn đi với **the**: *play the violin*.

exercises.question: Which is correct?
options: The poverty remains a major challenge.
A poverty remains a major challenge.
Poverty remains the major challenge for all the societies.
exercises.explanation: *poverty* không đếm được, dùng khái quát → không mạo từ; *societies* số nhiều khái quát cũng không mạo từ.

exercises.question: ___ more people move to cities, ___ greater the pressure on housing.
exercises.explanation: Cấu trúc **the more ..., the more ...** dùng *the* ở cả hai vế.

exercises.question: ___ prison where he served his sentence was built in 1890.
exercises.explanation: Ở đây nói về **tòa nhà** cụ thể → dùng *the*, khác với *sent to prison* (mục đích).

exercises.question: ___ elderly often face isolation in large cities.
exercises.explanation: **The elderly** = nhóm người cao tuổi, động từ chia số nhiều.

exercises.question: ___ conclusion of the report needs rewriting.
exercises.explanation: Có cụm *of the report* xác định rõ → dùng **the**, khác với cụm cố định *in conclusion*.

exercises.question: She is studying economics at ___ University of Hanoi.
exercises.explanation: Tên có cấu trúc **the ... of ...** luôn dùng *the*: *the University of Hanoi*, *the Bank of England*.
